description: Astronomy, Latin, architecture, robotics, Apollo history, science fiction, classical music, orbital mechanics, Elizabethan conspiracy, neuroscience and language carry the quiz from early 2025 into the first months of 2026.

s10e01.description: Stephen Fry faces questions on national treasures, U-turns, imperial pounds, octopus and squid ink, tennis seeds and the Addams Family before astronomy eventually explains the apparent twinkling of stars through scintillation.

s10e02.description: Anton Du Beke’s ladder includes toad in the hole, Cockneys, Eddie Stobart, humpback whales and Where’s Wally? before Latin legal vocabulary introduces pro bono.

s10e03.description: Julie Hesmondhalgh encounters grand pianos, ‘an open book’, eggplants, Cats, au pairs, baseball pitchers, baritones and Tiffany’s trademark blue before the questions travel to the distinctive Welsh village of Portmeirion.

s10e04.description: Steph McGovern’s questions move through airbags, quiche Lorraine, international football caps, woolly mammoths, Breaking Bad and Blackpool Illuminations before Cornwall’s Eden Project brings architecture and environmental science into the mix.

s10e05.description: Laura Kenny’s ladder covers duty-free shops, flamingos, ‘head to head’, spirits, Silicon Valley, kitten heels and Bonfire Night before robotics contributes the wonderfully technical term end effector.

s10e06.description: Time’s Person of the Year, ‘You Are Here’ maps, fairy lights, champagne and Germany’s Black Forest all appear alongside the Arsenal mascot Gunnersaurus. Space history eventually lands on Apollo 11’s Lunar Module Eagle.

s10e07.description: Dick Whittington, the Shanghai in HSBC, the wording of a British police caution and Neil Diamond’s Red Red Wine all surround a science-fiction stop with Arthur Dent from The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy.

s10e08.description: Famous statues are arranged from the Statue of Liberty to the Sphinx before Dracula, earworms, Newsround, mosaics, Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour and paleontology appear. Classical music then contributes Also Sprach Zarathustra.

s10e09.description: Roman numerals for 2025, the megalodon, yeast-free baking, Madame Doubtfire and the position of the tear glands precede an astronomy question defining perturbation: gravitational deviation from a regular orbit.

s10e10.description: African cities, potholes, pickling in vinegar, Roald Dahl’s BFG, platinum-blonde hair and Plaid Cymru all appear before Elizabethan conspiracy takes centre stage with the Babington Plot.

s10e11.description: County Cork, Holden Caulfield, Epsom salts and which events belong to the eighteenth century all precede a question about the hypothalamus and its role in regulating heart rate and body temperature.

s10e12.description: Animals are arranged north to south before belly buttons, the Tab key, St Bernards, Le Cordon Bleu, SpongeBob and the cox in a rowing eight all appear. Language later contributes the fortunate accident of serendipity.

s10e13.description: Famous bridges, agony aunts, American sidewalks, the Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race, olive branches, Japanese yen, the Famous Five and the NATO phonetic alphabet all appear before the questions venture into precognition.

s10e14.description: DIY, iPads as tablets, the Magic Circle, centipedes, pesto, lion-bearing logos, Outnumbered and George V all appear before flight engineering introduces the bird-inspired ornithopter.

s10e15.description: A bipedal velociraptor, Pixar’s Brave under its working title The Bear and the Bow, Buxton and the Peak District, neptunium, Gareth Southgate’s clubs and Edvard Munch all share the ladder.

s10e16.description: Sally Rooney, British universities from north to south, the Thames in EastEnders, bacon rashers and ‘resting on your laurels’ all appear before later questions wander through ghost flights and the almond-rich baking mixture frangipane.

s10e17.description: The Woman in White and its multiple documents, the world’s seas arranged north to south, the distress call Mayday and the exercise-induced ‘stitch’ all appear before astronomy turns to the moons of Uranus.
